summary: Promote 16 previously source-attributed traditional medicinal-use descriptions into the searchable medicinal claims library with explicit treatment/evidence distinctions. No clinical proof implied, no new dosing advice, and maintain source-links to original World traditions records.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Traditionally used for dental discomfort and digestive complaints
practice_claims.reported_use: Kew documents long traditional use for dental discomfort and digestive complaints across several regions.
practice_claims.limitations: Regional use is documented broadly; a particular preparation cannot be attributed to a named community from this source. Do not use concentrated oil internally; can irritate/burn tissues. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Traditional support for digestive and skin complaints
practice_claims.reported_use: Historical Indian medicinal applications include digestion, topical skin care, and inflammation.
practice_claims.limitations: Turmeric culinary rhizome, topical paste and concentrated curcumin capsules are chemically and clinically different. Rhizome and concentrated curcumin are not equivalent. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Historical claims involving liver, digestive and skin disorders
practice_claims.reported_use: Traditional applications include liver disorders, dysentery, ulcers and inflammation.
practice_claims.limitations: These are descriptions of traditional indications, not evidence turmeric cures dysentery or liver disease. No equivalence to treatment of liver disease or dysentery. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.reported_use: Kew reports turmeric used historically to support digestion and for inflammation-related complaints.
practice_claims.limitations: Different Curcuma species have overlapping common names in Chinese medicine; verify botanical identity. Other Curcuma medicinal materials and common names can be confused. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Traditional digestive, pain and skin-related uses
practice_claims.reported_use: A literature review documents long-standing traditional applications for digestion, appetite, pain, and skin complaints.
practice_claims.limitations: The review includes many preclinical claims; this record is solely about historically reported use. Seed and seed oil have different exposure profiles. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Traditional support for vitality and resilience
practice_claims.preparation: Fresh, dried white or processed red root
practice_claims.reported_use: Ginseng has a traditional role as a calming agent and in practices associated with supporting resilience to stress.
practice_claims.limitations: “Adaptogen” is a traditional/functional label, not a quantified clinical effect. Processed red vs white ginseng have different preparations. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.tradition: Traditional Chinese Medicine / historical materia medica
practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Traditional qi-related, calming-mind and cough-related claims
practice_claims.reported_use: Classical Chinese sources associate lingzhi with replenishing qi, calming the mind, and relieving cough-related complaints.
practice_claims.limitations: The commercial name “reishi” can cover several Ganoderma species; do not assume all species share chemical composition or clinical effects. Reishi is a species complex and older specimens may be misclassified. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Historical use for low mood and sleep complaints
practice_claims.reported_use: Iranian scholars studying Avicenna and major Islamic medical texts report traditional indications for low mood and sleep.
practice_claims.limitations: This is a reconstruction from historical sources, separate from modern clinical trials. Stigma and standardized clinical extracts are not equivalent. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.tradition: Razi and broader Islamic traditional medicine
practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Classical medicinal claims involving pain and respiratory complaints
practice_claims.reported_use: A source-based survey of Islamic medicine texts reports historical uses for pain, inflammation, and breathing complaints.
practice_claims.limitations: Modern human efficacy depends on specific outcomes and preparations; this record is historical. Descriptive historical claims, not indications proven in clinical trials. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.reported_use: Historically used for fever and inflammatory complaints.
practice_claims.limitations: Traditional use not proof of clinical efficacy; no restricted practice described. Immature and mature fruits differ; avoid equating wind-heat to laboratory infection diagnosis. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Historical use of tubers for pain-related complaints
practice_claims.limitations: Clinical efficacy of each isolated alkaloid not established by traditional use. Isoquinoline alkaloid binding data do not prove pain treatment. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.preparation: Aqueous root tea reported; no instructions
practice_claims.limitations: Not proof of efficacy or safety; not a replacement for recommended malaria treatment Malaria requires timely evidence-based treatment. This historical record is not a recommendation to replace it. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.tradition: Ayurveda, Siddha and related documented traditions
practice_claims.preparation: traditional fruit-based herbal preparation; descriptive only
practice_claims.reported_use: Traditionally described in digestive and general tonic contexts, sometimes within multi-herb systems.
practice_claims.limitations: Historical use does not prove safety or efficacy; chemical assay cited elsewhere used galls rather than fruits. Galls chemical results cannot be assigned to fruit preparations without evidence. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Historical topical leaf poultices for ulcers and tumors
practice_claims.reported_use: Flora of Iraq records leaves applied as poultices on tumors and ulcers.
practice_claims.limitations: Historical poultice use must not be read as evidence of cancer treatment or safe application to open skin. Use on tumors/ulcers does not establish anticancer efficacy or safety on open skin. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Historical topical leaf applications for burns and sunburn
practice_claims.reported_use: Flora of Oman records traditional use of pounded leaves for burns and sunburn.
practice_claims.limitations: This record does not establish safety or benefit on burns; burns require proper first aid. Do not treat serious burns with unverified poultices. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.

practice_claims.tradition: Flora of Tropical East Africa: recorded practices
practice_claims.condition_or_goal: Recorded root uses for intestinal worms, digestive and respiratory complaints
practice_claims.reported_use: Regional ethnobotanical accounts include stomach complaints, intestinal worms and coughs.
practice_claims.limitations: Multiple local traditions are grouped by the Flora source; exact community and formulation must be verified before finer attribution. No demonstration of human deworming efficacy, safety or dose. Traditional medicine concepts are preserved as reported; no clinical efficacy is established by this record.
